sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **10 of the official questions in Cross-Text Connections are this one** — 2 Easy, 2 Medium, 6 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- Text 1 reasons from an observation to a cause ('found X... therefore concluded Y').
- Text 2 re-examines the same material, often with a new or higher-resolution method, and names another thing that could produce X.
- These are mostly Hard, and the passages are dense with technical terms.
- Choices often read like 'the evidence Text 1 relies on may reflect something other than...'.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Split Text 1 into its observation and the inference drawn from it.
- 2) Find the alternative source of that observation that Text 2 identifies.
- 3) Pick the choice saying the observation doesn't necessarily support Text 1's inference.
- Don't pick one that denies the observation happened.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You pick a choice saying Text 1's data or measurement was wrong.
In fact Text 2 accepts the observation and only attacks what was inferred from it.
Choices that repeat technical words from Text 2 without the 'alternative cause' logic are the other bait.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You pick a choice saying Text 1's data or measurement was wrong.
In fact Text 2 accepts the observation and only attacks what was inferred from it.
